supported_interpretation: Explicit safe rule alone did not guarantee safe-optimal allocation in the observed harmful-note condition.
All three partial-harm outcomes occur with notes present and reminder absent; one role chooses its original harmful-note task while the partner implements the shared rule.
Stated final reasons cite the handoff/prior convention in the failing role: behavioural and self-report evidence, not access to internal decision processes.
The reminder improves observed safe-optimal completion under these harmful notes, conditional on the supplied rule; both note-absent arms show observed ceiling performance.
necessary_limits: Three failures occur in only two model-case pairs. The entire GPT interaction arises from one donor case across both fixed directions.
Note treatment includes its entire text, useful information and wording; not a pure manipulation of harmfulness.
No general necessity, statistical significance, or individual stochastic-error causation claim.
GPT point estimate1/5 uses five common complete cases; its logical interval[1/6,1/4] concerns all six available cases, is not a confidence interval, and does not bound broader generalization.
Reminder effect is on partial harm and safe optimality, not binary joint harm; all valid new episodes have zero binary joint harm.
No new legitimate-note condition; useful-cooperation evidence remains from earlier studies.
